name: AI SEO Masterclass - Module 6 Parasite SEO
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-08

# Summary
Parasite SEO means publishing on high-authority platforms you do not own (Reddit, Medium, LinkedIn, Quora, YouTube, Substack, Facebook Groups, press release sites, web 2.0s) to borrow their authority. The author says Google's 2024 site reputation abuse actions hit lazy abuse of news domains, not the tactic itself.

# Platform notes (as taught)
- **Reddit (DR 91):** cited in a large share of AI Overviews, indexes in hours. Structure: personal story, journey, solution, numbers, resources, ask for comments.
- **Medium (DR 95):** 1,500 to 2,500 words, "Best X" or how-to, submit to publications.
- **LinkedIn (DR 98):** B2B articles, no affiliate links, drive to lead magnets.
- **Quora (DR 90):** answer high-view questions, direct answer first, 500+ words.
- **YouTube (DR 100):** chapters, transcript, description summary for AI Overviews.

# Dual-ranking structure
Title with keyword and year, "Quick answer" block, 200-word intro, 1,500+ word body with pros/cons and tables, 8 to 12 FAQs with schema, conclusion, "Last updated" date. Refresh monthly.

# Monetization and risk
Affiliate, lead gen, own offers, ad revenue, consulting leads. Risks: deletion, policy changes, algorithm shifts, bans. Mitigation: spread across 5+ platforms, keep backups, build an email list, do not build a whole business on parasites.

# How this applies to TAG clients
- TAG caution: this course mixes white-hat basics with gray-hat and black-hat tactics. Anything that fakes reviews, fakes accounts, manipulates votes or builds link networks breaks Google, Reddit or FTC rules and is not something to run on a client brand. Claims in client copy must stay backed by the live site, the owner or Scott ([SEO Blog Writing Standards](lib:brain-seo-blog-writing-standards)).
- The lesson recommends buying aged accounts, upvoting with alt accounts and editing links in after moderation; those break platform rules and are excluded.
- Legit takeaways: a real company LinkedIn or Medium article that summarizes a client blog (with a canonical link back), genuine YouTube how-to videos, and answer-first formatting.
